Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

parqeye

parqeye lets you peek inside Parquet files. Instantly inspect their contents, schema, and metadata right from your terminal.

Features

- Interactive Data Visualization: Browse your Parquet data in a table view with keyboard navigation.
- Schema Explorer: Inspect column types, nested structures, and field definitions.
- File Metadata: View Parquet file-level metadata including version, "created by", encoding stats and more.
- Row Group Statistics: Examine row group-level metadata, statistics, and data distribution across groups.
- Tab-based Interface: Quickly switch between Visualize, Schema, Metadata, and Row Groups views.
- Terminal-native: Works directly in your terminal.

Usage

Run the tool by providing the path to a .parquet file:

    parqeye <path-to-parquet-file>

Installation

Download the latest release from the project's Releases page or use a platform package manager if available.

License

This project is released under the MIT License. See the LICENSE file for details.

    for l in lines:
        print(l)
    print(f"--- END {label} ---\n")
    return r.stdout

b0c96a9 Initial commit
parqeye

parqeye lets you peek inside Parquet files. Instantly inspect their contents, schema, and metadata right from your terminal.

Features

- Interactive Data Visualization: Browse your Parquet data in a table view with keyboard navigation.
- Schema Explorer: Inspect column types, nested structures, and field definitions.
- File Metadata: View Parquet file-level metadata including version, "created by", encoding stats and more.
- Row Group Statistics: Examine row group-level metadata, statistics, and data distribution across groups.
- Tab-based Interface: Quickly switch between Visualize, Schema, Metadata, and Row Groups views.
- Terminal-native: Works directly in your terminal.

Usage

Run the tool by providing the path to a .parquet file:

    parqeye <path-to-parquet-file>

Installation

Download the latest release from the project's Releases page or use a platform package manager if available.

subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-x","250","-y","50","-s",session], check=True)
time.sleep(0.5)

def start_file(path):
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",session, f"./executable {path}", "Enter"], check=True)
    time.sleep(1.2)

def capture():
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-p","-t",session], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout

def send(k,w=0.6):
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",session,k], check=True)
    time.sleep(w)

# capture all assets sequentially
files=sorted([os.path.join("assets",f) for f in os.listdir("assets") if f.endswith(".parquet")])
for path in files:
    start_file(path)
    # visualize
    out_vis=capture()
    # go metadata
    send("Tab")
    out_meta=capture()
    # schema
    send("Tab")
    out_schema=capture()
    # row groups
    send("Tab")
    out_rg=capture()
    # Write summary
    print(f"\n===== {path} =====")
    print("---VIS---")
    # first few lines of vis table
    for l in out_vis.splitlines()[2:12]:
        print(l)
    print("---META---")
    for l in out_meta.splitlines():
        if "File Metadata" in l or "Format version" in l or "Created by" in l or "Rows" in l or "Columns" in l or "Row groups" in l or "Size" in l or "Compression ratio" in l or "Codecs" in l or "Encodings" in l or "Avg row size" in l:
            print(l)
    print("---SCHEMA TREE FIRST 20---")
    for l in out_schema.splitlines()[2:22]:
        print(l)
    print("---RG---")
    for l in out_rg.splitlines()[2:20]:
        print(l)
    send("q")
    time.sleep(0.3)

subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",session])

import subprocess, time, re
session="parqeye_test"
subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",session], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-x","60","-y","20","-s",session], check=True)
time.sleep(0.5)
subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",session,"bash --noprofile --norc --noediting","Enter"], check=True)
time.sleep(0.5)

def start_file(p):
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",session,f"./executable {p}","Enter"], check=True)
    time.sleep(1.2)

def capture_esc():
    return subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-p","-e","-t",session], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout

def send(k,w=0.6):
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",session,k], check=True)
    time.sleep(w)

def clear():
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t",session,"clear","Enter"], check=True)
    time.sleep(0.3)

def parse_selected(esc):
    # find line with background 60;60;60 and extract row number
    for line in esc.splitlines():
        if "60;60;60" in line:
            m=re.search(r'\[1;4m.*?(\d+)', line)
            # actually pattern: \x1b[1;4m<rownum>
            m2=re.search(r'\[1;4m\x1b\[38;5;8m(\d+)', line)
            m3=re.search(r'\[1;4m(\d+)', line)
            # try simpler: split
            # The row number is before pipe, with underline
            # Extract digit at start after escape
            # Use regex \d+.*│
            mm=re.search(r'(\d+)\s+│', line)
            if mm:
                # but there may be two numbers? The row number is first number before │
                # We'll extract first number in line that is before │
                left=line.split('│')[0]
                nums=re.findall(r'\d+', left)
                if nums:
                    return nums[0]
    return None

def first_visible(plain):
    for line in plain.splitlines():
        if "│" in line:
            left=line.split("│")[0].strip()
            token=left.split()[0] if left.split() else ""
            if token.isdigit():
                return token

# We need to decide implementation language.
# Rust seems best because original is Rust, and we have ratatui and crossterm cached.
# We can implement parquet parsing in pure Rust without external crates.
# Let's attempt to implement minimal parquet reader that handles our observed behavior.

# Parquet file format basics:
# - File ends with 8 bytes: 4 bytes footer length (little endian u32) + 4 bytes magic "PAR1"
# - Footer is Thrift compact protocol serialized FileMetaData
# - FileMetaData contains: version, num_rows, created_by, row_groups, etc., plus schema (list of SchemaElement)
# We need to parse Thrift compact protocol.
# Apache Parquet Thrift definition: https://github.com/apache/parquet-format/blob/master/src/main/thrift/parquet.thrift
# We can implement compact protocol decoder for the structures we need.

# Let's inspect parquet file footer manually to understand encoding.
# We'll write a python script to read last bytes and attempt to decode thrift compact.

import struct, os, sys

def read_footer(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        f.seek(-8, os.SEEK_END)
        tail=f.read(8)
        magic=tail[4:]
        flen=struct.unpack('<I', tail[:4])[0]
        print(f"{path} magic {magic} footer len {flen}")
        f.seek(-(8+flen), os.SEEK_END)
        footer_bytes=f.read(flen)
        print(f" footer first 100 bytes: {footer_bytes[:100]}")
        # try to check if it starts with thrift compact protocol struct?
        # For FileMetaData: field 1 = version (i32), field 2 = schema list, etc.
        # Compact protocol: struct begins with implicit.
        # Let's dump hex for alltypes_plain.parquet footer.
        # Write to file for later analysis
        open('/tmp/footer.bin','wb').write(footer_bytes)
        return footer_bytes

fb=read_footer('assets/alltypes_plain.parquet')

# Let's attempt to implement compact protocol reading in python quickly to see if we can parse.
# Thrift compact protocol spec:
# - Struct: sequence of fields, each field header: (field_id delta + type)

parqeye

parqeye lets you peek inside Parquet files. Instantly inspect their contents, schema, and metadata right from your terminal.

Features

- Interactive Data Visualization: Browse your Parquet data in a table view with keyboard navigation.
- Schema Explorer: Inspect column types, nested structures, and field definitions.
- File Metadata: View Parquet file-level metadata including version, "created by", encoding stats and more.
- Row Group Statistics: Examine row group-level metadata, statistics, and data distribution across groups.
- Tab-based Interface: Quickly switch between Visualize, Schema, Metadata, and Row Groups views.
- Terminal-native: Works directly in your terminal.

Usage

Run the tool by providing the path to a .parquet file:

    parqeye <path-to-parquet-file>

Installation

Download the latest release from the project's Releases page or use a platform package manager if available.

License

This project is released under the MIT License. See the LICENSE file for details.

Acknowledgements

- csvlens for inspiration

use std::path::PathBuf;

mod thrift;
mod parquet;
mod decompress;
mod encoding;
mod ui;
mod data;

fn main() {
    let matches = Command::new("parqeye")
        .about("Command line tool to visualize parquet files")
        .version("0.0.2")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("PATH")
                .help("Path to the parquet file")
                .required(true)
                .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(PathBuf)),
        )
        .get_matches();

    let path = matches.get_one::<PathBuf>("PATH").unwrap();

    // Try to open file and check parquet
    match open_parquet(path) {
        Ok(()) => {}
        Err(e) => {
            // Print in same format as original: "Error: Custom { kind: Other, error: \"...\" }"
            eprintln!("{}", e);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }

    // If file is valid, attempt to read metadata and data
    let file_result = data::read_parquet_file(path);
    let parquet_file = match file_result {
        Ok(f) => f,
        Err(err_msg) => {
            // For parquet errors, original prints same format
            let io_err = std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, err_msg);
            eprintln!("Error: {}", io_err);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    };

    // Launch TUI
    if let Err(e) = ui::run(parquet_file) {
        eprintln!("Error running UI: {}", e);
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
}

fn open_parquet(path: &std::path::Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    // Check file exists
    match std::fs::File::open(path) {
        Ok(file) => {
            // Try to validate parquet footer quickly
            let metadata = std::fs::metadata(path).map_err(|e| format!("Error: {}", std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, format!("{} (os error {})", e, e.raw_os_error().unwrap_or(0)))))?;
            if metadata.len() < 8 {
                let msg = "Parquet error: Invalid Parquet file. Corrupt footer".to_string();
                return Err(format!("Error: {}", std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, msg)));
            }
            let mut f = file;
            use std::io::{Seek, SeekFrom, Read};
            f.seek(SeekFrom::End(-8)).map_err(|e| format!("Error: {}", e))?;
            let mut tail = [0u8; 8];
            f.read_exact(&mut tail).map_err(|e| format!("Error: {}", e))?;
            let magic = &tail[4..];
            if magic != b"PAR1" && magic != b"PARE" {
                let msg = "Parquet error: Invalid Parquet file. Corrupt footer".to_string();
                return Err(format!("Error: {}", std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, msg)));
            }
            if magic == b"PARE" {
                let msg = "Parquet error: Parquet file has an encrypted footer but the encryption feature is disabled".to_string();
                return Err(format!("Error: {}", std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, msg)));
            }
            // Check footer length and try to parse? We already handled encrypted case via magic PARE? Actually encrypted files still have PAR1 magic? Let's check earlier: encrypted file had magic PARE, so we catch.
            // For invalid file (README.md), magic not PAR1 => corrupt footer
            Ok(())
        }
        Err(e) => {
            // Original format: "Error: Custom { kind: Other, error: \"No such file or directory (os error 2)\" }"
            // In Rust, io::Error Display for custom error shows "Custom { kind: Other, error: \"...\" }" when using custom error?
            // Let's create custom error with same message as underlying
            let msg = format!("{} (os error {})", e, e.raw_os_error().unwrap_or(0));
            let custom = std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, msg);
            Err(format!("Error: {}", custom))
        }
    }
}

fn open_parquet(path: &std::path::Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    match std::fs::File::open(path) {
        Ok(file) => {
            let metadata = std::fs::metadata(path).map_err(|e| {
                let msg = format!("{} (os error {})", e, e.raw_os_error().unwrap_or(0));
                let custom = std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, msg);
                format!("Error: {}", custom)
            })?;
            if metadata.len() < 8 {
                let msg = "Parquet error: Invalid Parquet file. Corrupt footer".to_string();
                return Err(format!("Error: {}", std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, msg)));
            }
            let mut f = file;
            use std::io::{Seek, SeekFrom, Read};
            f.seek(SeekFrom::End(-8)).map_err(|e| format!("Error: {}", e))?;
            let mut tail = [0u8; 8];
            f.read_exact(&mut tail).map_err(|e| format!("Error: {}", e))?;
            let magic = &tail[4..];
            if magic != b"PAR1" && magic != b"PARE" {
                let msg = "Parquet error: Invalid Parquet file. Corrupt footer".to_string();
                return Err(format!("Error: {}", std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, msg)));
            }
            if magic == b"PARE" {
                let msg = "Parquet error: Parquet file has an encrypted footer but the encryption feature is disabled".to_string();
                return Err(format!("Error: {}", std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, msg)));
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        Err(e) => {
            let msg = format!("{} (os error {})", e, e.raw_os_error().unwrap_or(0));
            let custom = std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::Other, msg);
            Err(format!("Error: {}", custom))
        }
    }
}

fn get_visualize_visible_rows(term_height: usize) -> usize {
    if term_height <= 6 { return 1; }
    term_height - 6
}

fn flatten_schema_tree(tree: &[SchemaNode]) -> Vec<usize> {
    let mut flat = Vec::new();
    if tree.is_empty() { return flat; }
    let mut stack = vec![0];
    while let Some(idx) = stack.pop() {
        flat.push(idx);
        for &child in tree[idx].children.iter().rev() {
            stack.push(child);
        }
    }
    flat
}

fn draw_column_statistics(f: &mut Frame, area: Rect, app: &mut App) {
    let flat = &app.schema.flat_nodes;
    let nodes_to_show: Vec<usize> = flat.iter().skip(1).cloned().collect();

    let header_titles = vec!["Repetition", "Physical", "Compressed", "Uncompressed", "Ratio", "Encodings", "Compression", "Min", "Max", "Nulls"];
    let scroll = app.schema.scroll;

    let header_cells: Vec<Cell> = header_titles.iter().enumerate().filter(|(i,_)| *i >= scroll).map(|(_, t)| Cell::from(*t).style(Style::default().fg(Color::Yellow).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD))).collect();
    let header = Row::new(header_cells).height(1);

    let mut rows = Vec::new();
    for (flat_idx, &node_idx) in nodes_to_show.iter().enumerate() {
        if node_idx >= app.file.schema_tree.len() { continue; }
        let node = &app.file.schema_tree[node_idx];
        let is_selected = flat_idx + 1 == app.schema.selected;

        let col_chunk_opt = if node.is_leaf {
            app.file.metadata.row_groups.first().and_then(|rg| rg.columns.iter().find(|c| c.meta_data.path_in_schema == node.path))
        } else { None };

        let mut fields = Vec::new();
        fields.push(node.repetition.clone());
        fields.push(node.physical_type.clone());
        fields.push(col_chunk_opt.map(|c| format_size(c.meta_data.total_compressed_size)).unwrap_or_default());
        fields.push(col_chunk_opt.map(|c| format_size(c.meta_data.total_uncompressed_size)).unwrap_or_default());
        fields.push(col_chunk_opt.map(|c| if c.meta_data.total_uncompressed_size>0 { format!("{:.2}x", c.meta_data.total_compressed_size as f64 / c.meta_data.total_uncompressed_size as f64) } else { "".to_string() }).unwrap_or_default());
        fields.push(col_chunk_opt.map(|c| c.meta_data.encodings.iter().map(|&e| encoding_name(e)).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")).unwrap_or_default());
        fields.push(col_chunk_opt.map(|c| compression_name(c.meta_data.codec)).unwrap_or_default());
        fields.push(col_chunk_opt.and_then(|c| c.meta_data.statistics.as_ref()).and_then(|s| s.min.as_ref()).map(|b| format_byte_array_min_max(b)).unwrap_or_else(|| "NULL".to_string()));
        fields.push(col_chunk_opt.and_then(|c| c.meta_data.statistics.as_ref()).and_then(|s| s.max.as_ref()).map(|b| format_byte_array_min_max(b)).unwrap_or_else(|| "NULL".to_string()));
        fields.push(col_chunk_opt.and_then(|c| c.meta_data.statistics.as_ref()).and_then(|s| s.null_count).map(|n| n.to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|| "0".to_string()));

        let cells: Vec<Cell> = fields.into_iter().enumerate().filter(|(i,_)| *i >= scroll).map(|(_, f)| {
            let style = if is_selected { Style::default().fg(Color::Black).bg(Color::Yellow) } else { Style::default() };
            Cell::from(f).style(style)
        }).collect();

        rows.push(Row::new(cells).height(1));
    }

fn format_byte_array_min_max(data: &[u8]) -> String {
    if let Ok(s) = std::str::from_utf8(data) {
        if s.chars().all(|c| c.is_alphanumeric() || c.is_whitespace() || "!\"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\\]^_`{|}~".contains(c)) {
            return s.to_string();
        }
    }
    if data.len() == 4 {
        return i32::from_le_bytes([data[0],data[1],data[2],data[3]]).to_string();
    }
    if data.len() == 8 {
        return i64::from_le_bytes([data[0],data[1],data[2],data[3],data[4],data[5],data[6],data[7]]).to_string();
    }
    format!("{:?}", data)
}

fn decompress_snappy(input: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    fn read_varint(buf: &[u8]) -> Option<(usize, usize)> {
        let mut result: usize = 0;
        let mut shift = 0;
        let mut pos = 0;
        for _ in 0..10 {
            if pos >= buf.len() { return None; }
            let b = buf[pos];
            pos += 1;
            result |= ((b & 0x7f) as usize) << shift;
            if (b & 0x80) == 0 { return Some((result, pos)); }
            shift += 7;
        }
        None
    }

    let (uncompressed_len, header_len) = match read_varint(input) {
        Some(v) => v,
        None => (0, 0),
    };

    let compressed_data = if header_len > 0 && header_len < 10 {
        &input[header_len..]
    } else {
        input
    };

    decompress_snappy_raw(compressed_data, uncompressed_len)
}

fn decompress_snappy_raw(input: &[u8], _expected_len: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let mut output = Vec::with_capacity(1024);
    let mut pos = 0;
    while pos < input.len() {
        let tag = input[pos];
        pos += 1;
        let tag_type = tag & 0x03;
        if tag_type == 0 {
            let mut len = (tag >> 2) as usize;
            if len < 60 {
                len += 1;
            } else {
                let extra = (len - 60 + 1) as usize;
                if pos + extra > input.len() { return Err("snappy literal length overflow".to_string()); }
                let mut l = 0usize;
                for i in 0..extra {
                    l |= (input[pos + i] as usize) << (8 * i);
                }
                pos += extra;
                len = l + 1;
            }
            if pos + len > input.len() {
                return Err(format!("snappy literal data overflow: pos {} len {} input len {}", pos, len, input.len()));
            }
            output.extend_from_slice(&input[pos..pos+len]);
            pos += len;
        } else {
            let (copy_len, offset) = match tag_type {
                1 => {
                    let len = ((tag >> 2) & 0x07) as usize + 4;
                    if pos >= input.len() { return Err("snappy copy 1-byte offset missing".to_string()); }
                    let offset = (((tag as usize) >> 5) << 8) | (input[pos] as usize);
                    pos += 1;
                    (len, offset)
                },
                2 => {
                    let len = ((tag >> 2) as usize) + 4;
                    if pos + 2 > input.len() { return Err("snappy copy 2-byte offset missing".to_string()); }
                    let offset = (input[pos] as usize) | ((input[pos+1] as usize) << 8);
                    pos += 2;
                    (len, offset)
                },
                3 => {
                    let len = ((tag >> 2) as usize) + 4;
                    if pos + 4 > input.len() { return Err("snappy copy 4-byte offset missing".to_string()); }
                    let offset = (input[pos] as usize) | ((input[pos+1] as usize) << 8) | ((input[pos+2] as usize) << 16) | ((input[pos+3] as usize) << 24);
                    pos += 4;
                    (len, offset)
                },
                _ => unreachable!(),
            };
            if offset == 0 || offset > output.len() {
                return Err(format!("snappy invalid offset {} output len {}", offset, output.len()));
            }
            let start = output.len() - offset;
            for i in 0..copy_len {
                let b = output[start + i];
                output.push(b);
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(output)
}

    use std::ffi::CString;
    use std::os::raw::{c_void, c_char};

    const RTLD_NOW: i32 = 2;

    extern "C" {
        fn dlopen(filename: *const c_char, flag: i32) -> *mut c_void;
        fn dlsym(handle: *mut c_void, symbol: *const c_char) -> *mut c_void;
    }

    unsafe {
        let lib_name = CString::new("/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/liblz4.so.1").unwrap();

        if handle.is_null() {

        }

        let sym = CString::new("LZ4_decompress_safe").unwrap();
        let fn_ptr = dlsym(handle, sym.as_ptr());
        if fn_ptr.is_null() {
            return Err("dlsym LZ4_decompress_safe failed".to_string());
        }

        // Guess output size as input*10 or 1M
        let output_size = input.len() * 10 + 1024;
        let mut output = vec![0u8; output_size];

        type Lz4Fn = unsafe extern "C" fn(*const u8, *mut u8, i32, i32) -> i32;
        let lz4_fn: Lz4Fn = std::mem::transmute(fn_ptr);

            return Err(format!("LZ4 decompress error {}", ret));
        }

fn build_schema_tree(schema: &[crate::parquet::SchemaElement]) -> Result<Vec<SchemaNode>, String> {
    if schema.is_empty() { return Err("empty schema".to_string()); }

    struct StackItem { idx: usize, remaining: i32, }

    let mut nodes: Vec<SchemaNode> = Vec::new();
    let mut stack: Vec<StackItem> = Vec::new();

    for (i, elem) in schema.iter().enumerate() {
        let name = elem.name.clone();
        let repetition = elem.repetition.map(|r| repetition_str(r)).unwrap_or_else(|| "".to_string());
        let physical = elem.r#type.map(|t| physical_type_str(t)).unwrap_or_else(|| "group".to_string());
        let is_leaf = elem.num_children.is_none();

        let parent_path = if let Some(parent) = stack.last() {
            nodes[parent.idx].path.clone()
        } else { Vec::new() };

    Ok(out)
}
